title: App keeps closing and sometimes doesn’t register finished routines

title: Just what I needed
text: Excellent for ADHD, time blindness and procrastination. I tend to make a list, do 1 or 2 out of 10 things, sit on the couch and then feel awful about myself later on. This app gives you a full customized visual schedule, audio reminders and a visual timer so that you are 100% on top of your day. The timer is really the life changing aspect, I put every single task in this app (eat, shower, etc) because as my fellow NDs know, you can procrastinate anything and everything for hours on end and not even notice the time.  I enjoy picking the little icons out and organizing my routine so it provides some enjoyment which motivates me to open the app in the mornings. Very user friendly. I also like how I can build in new things I want to incorporate into my routine such as exercise. If I see a new task and a timer, I am more likely to try the new task because I set designated time aside for it, rather than looking at the new task and scratching it off my list.

title: Weight check?
text: I started setting up my morning routine and one of the suggested activities is a weight check, saying “check your weight changes daily.” I did this for years and it is extremely psychologically damaging, to anyone. This can caused disordered eating & obsessive behaviors that are never healthy. For an app advertised to people with ADHD, this is dangerous and can cause fixation. ADHDers are prone to disordered eating already, from food fixations, forgetting to eat, meds killing appetite, executive dysfunction when it comes to cooking, etc. It takes a long time for a lot of us to hack these things and learn to feed our bodies, and fixating on daily weight changes can be so destructive to our mental and physical health. Weight≠health

title: 좋아요! 근데
text:
정말 잘 쓰고 있고 앱도 너무 예뻐서 만족도가 높습니다! 딱 세 가지만 추가 된다면 오래오래 구독하고 사용할 것 같습니다. 

 1. 루틴을 시작하는 시간을 설정하는게 아니라 끝내야 하는 시간을 설정하는 방식도 추가해주세요! 그래서 그 시간까지 루틴을 끝내기 위해서 언제 시작해야 하는지 알려주는 기능, 그리고 어떤 항목이 조금씩 시간이 더 걸려서 밀리게 되면 다음 루틴들은 그만큼 시간을 줄여서 하도록 나왔으면 합니다. 사실 다른 앱에 있는 기능인데 루티너리가 너무 예뻐서 여기에 꼭 있었으면 좋겠어요! ( 예: ‘물마시기’가 원래 3분이 걸려야 시간에 맞게 끝낼 수 있는데 5분이 걸렸다. 그러면 그 뒤에 있는 명상하기, 세수하기 등 에 쓸 수 있는 시간이 조금씩 단축되어 제시간에 맞게 끝낼 수 있도록 저절로 설정된다.) 

 2. 아이콘 검색 기능 추가해주세요! 아이콘이 너무 많다보니 하나하나 확인하고 고르기 힘든데 검색 기능이 있다면 좋을 것 같아요.

3. 루틴 속에 있는 항목을 하나하나 끝낼 때마다 좀 더 시각적으로나 청각적으로 효과가 있었으면 좋겠어요. 좀 더 뿌듯하도록! 일단 당장 생각나는 것은 항목을 끝내고 확인을 누를 때마다 효과음이 났으면 좋겠습니다.

title: I need checklists
text:
Almost perfect! I love the nagging reminders. Helps me manage my ADHD. However I sometimes find super granular, linear steps to be too rigid. I prefer being able to have a step contain a collection of smaller tasks, like Oral Care having flossing, brushing, and mouthwashing. I can add the text for that in the step’s Context area, but I would much prefer being able to mark them off in the order I complete them in a nice list. Tiimo does this checklist feature so well and even with Apple Watch, but misses the mark on the manual start and nagging reminders that this app excels at.

I will keep looking for an app that does all those things (will happy pay for it) until this app incorporates checklists. Unfortunately the developer’s app update release notes don’t appear to include details on what was edited in the app, just general comments to the user base, so I’m unsure if this app is continuing to develop or is just in stasis.

title: Could be a life changer but?
text:
I just got this app and am setting up my morning routine. I can see how much it would help me with my ADHD/time blindness! The only problem is there are no instructions or tutorials. I’ve read reviews of people talking about things they’re doing with this app. I only wish I knew how to do them. There's urprisingly nothing useable on YouTube! It’s very odd because clearly they put in a ton of clinical research and show a great understanding of ADHD core problems. 

Is there a way to search all of the included habits? No idea but I hope so. For now I’m just finding things randomly in the limited categories (morning, night, Oprah Winfrey, Healthy) which are incomplete at best. So I'm sure there must be another way.

I'd like to set a morning routine that includes everyday tasks that I can add certain chores to on different days. Again, I'm sure you can do this but there's no way to find out.

I got a month of premium membership but again, I didn't get any information on how to use it. TBH I'm not even sure what it includes.  I figured for $2.99 I'd have time to see if it was worth it.

Overall, I see a lot of potential but I'll have to add "Try to figure out how to use this app, 30 minutes" as a habit if I want to really benefit, which is the opposite of what a person with ADHD needs. In fact, I'm getting overwhelmed just thinking abouthow many steps there will be to finish this one routine without knowing the right way to do it.

I suspect the developers had this incredible idea and they took it live before it was really complete, which is exactly what most of us with ADHD would do! I have reached out to them for help and hopefully they’ll get back to me with answers to some of my specific questions. So basically, it’s a really great app with room for improvement.

My main struggle is forgetfulness and this app solves that completely. You can make variations for different days that have different schedules. This app will help you stay on track for all your goals. One of the best things about this app is focusing on the small things like making your bed. Making your bed is such a insignificant thing that people like me forget over and over to do it. Through this app though I remember every single day to do the simple things. The pricing is so cheap for how much this app can change your life. With all the sincerity thank you 🙏 😊 developer for creating this wonderful app.

text: So far loving this app! I like that it doesn't automatically start at the time I set it for, so if I sleep in I can still start my routine when I'm ready. It connects to my smart watch as well, so if I'm still in bed and not on my phone, I get an extra notification. I like how customizable it is. This seems to be really handy for my ADHD, and I'm getting out of the door on time too! I don't like the "gone over the time" countdown after you've run out of time on a task, because it seems like it could feel punitive, but it does help to adjust my routine to accommodate for the reality of how much time certain tasks take. Overall, I'm okay with paying for this app because of how much it improves my quality of life! And the little encouragements every time I open the app are very sweet as well.

text: I’ve only had the app for a few days and it’s honestly already improved my life so much. I have ADD and I’ve struggled with “time blindness” most of my life. title: Great concept, but very laggy and frustrating
text: This is a great asset for anyone who needs a lite help with routines in life. However, the app's performance lags often during basic functions. I'm not sure why, as the app surely can't be resource intensive and is the only app that I have had this problem with. Examples include 4-5 second delays when starting the next activity, erroneous notifications for activities you already moved on from (drives me pretty nuts), and being unable to edit your routine finishing times. This last one breaks the "average time" stat because often forget to complete the last activity in a routine. In a gym app like Strong, for example, forgetting to close out the session is no problem because you can edit the end time. I am not sure why these kinds of basic features are missing, but they are really frustrating and marr an otherwise great app in my experience. I appreciate the work that has been done so far though.

title: Best app for sticking to a routine
text:
I’ve tried several routine apps. I like this one best because it is simple and is really focussed on routines, not trying to do a lot of other stuff as well. 

Three things would make it a five star app for me:

- A single tap to start a routine. At the moment it is a couple of taps. I need routines in my life because I’m so easily distracted, so getting started quickly is essential. 
- Better Apple Watch synchronisation. At the moment it is in beta and quite flaky. 
- Being able to have some steps only show up on certain days (e.g. I only need to water plants twice a week)

It’s still the best routine app without those features but I feel it will be complete for me when it has them.

title: Really worth it! 1-2 bugs
text:
I love this app, as an ADHDer I have a hard time sticking to routines and this app has actually kept my interest/motivation for months now :) It’s exactly what I need to get me going in the mornings, to simplify the decision making process and keep me moving from task to task. A couple of issues though, which I’d love to see fixed!

- the main one is that it is SO SLOW and glitchy. If you try to check off/skip more than one task within 10 seconds, it freezes for at least that amount of time. Also uses a HUGE chunk of my battery which is an issue especially in the mornings when I find myself leaving for work with my phone at 60-70% (down from 100%) after doing a 1hr routine. No reason in the world that a simple habit tracker should require so much power to run in the background!! Please fix!

- I would love the ability to change the order and add/skip events while you’re in a routine. It only gives you the option to rearrange one list item at a time, when you’re currently supposed to be doing that item. Especially since the app is slow, this takes way too long if I want to check off a later task during the routine I have to skip every single task before it, in order, while waiting for it to stop freezing up. Torture.

- a feature I’d love to see: setting an end time for the routine. Eg. I want to say “finish this routine by 8:55am” and have it remind me what time to start the routine. Maybe even condense the list items if I’m running behind, like automatically reducing the “breakfast” item from 15 minutes to 12 minutes if I’m running late. I love this app but it still doesn’t quite get me out the door on time since there is far too much flexibility to pause or go over the time limits… 🙄 lol

Overall I think it’s still worth using!! After less than a week I splurged and paid for the full version and I still don’t regret it, this is one of the ones I could immediately tell would be worth it. Genius concept and thank you so much for designing this ❤️

title: Huge potential; nagging issues
text:
This app is a great idea, has many well thought out features, and I can see it being an indispensable part of my life. I bought premium immediately. By far the best way to use it is with Apple Watch, though the phone app is absolutely necessary for designing the routines. 

Major issues:
- Any music playing stops when you start a routine on the phone app
- Apple Watch app sends THREE loud notifications when you need to switch tasks, two overlapping each other and one with a totally different sound. It sounds rather bad!
- Apple Watch app has sync issues. Oftentimes in the morning will show all my routines as completed, sometimes gets stuck in a weird state

Love:
- Estimated end time on routines. I struggle with time blindness and it blows my mind every day that my morning routine takes 20 minutes even though each action is under two minutes. 
- Records of start and end times of routines, and how much over or under you were on each task, for every routine you’ve ever completed.
- Attractive UI. 
- Clear explanations for what most settings do.
- Tasks you add are saved, so you can add the same task to other routines with one click. 
- Timer effect on each task (if you’ve used the physical time timer, it’s like that)
- notes and feedback on routines (so you can remember what you want to change later)
- repeated notifications are available if you’ve gone over time on a task or paused it. Indispensable if you get distracted easily 
- suggested routines (find them under “Explore” when adding a new routine)
- home screen widgets available 

Top suggestions for quality of life improvements:
- Faster options for moving a task to the end of a routine. For example, swipe up on the task card to send it to the end. Right now this requires 2-3 clicks. 
- Icon search when adding icons to tasks (or option to use regular emojis as the icon, since iOS keyboard has search built in)
- More obvious/colorful full timer effect on tasks, so the disappearing timer is easily visible from farther away

title: OUTSTANDING! Best of its kind.
text:
Dozens of productivity apps have failed me before I found Routinery. Most productivity apps actually make us less productive because they require the user to exercise perfect judgment when making scheduling decisions. Those apps make it too easy to feel good in the moment when we create a new task... but those apps fail to account for the fact that people often don't do what they say they are going to do. On stressful or lazy days I ended up doing what was most convenient. 

Routinery is the ONLY app that has worked for me because it is convenient! The UI/UX reduces the amount of effort required to create a new routine. It lessens the barriers between activites I want to do more often by making it more convenient for me to start them and do them.I noticed improvements right away!

Routinery is the only productivity app with a "Recommended Routines" feature. There are a few dozen curated routines for Morning, Afternoon, Night, Productivity, Famous People's Routines, etc.It's so easy to just start from one of these (instead of having to spend an hour coming up with a routine on my own, I'd much rather start from popular examples). if you want to start a new routine you can also use their templates of individual tasks. The individual task templates also correspond to a specific time which is SOOO convenient. (So I don't have to think about each and every task and ask myself, how much time does it take me to do this?)

With previous to-do apps, I used to spend a couple of hours writing down my vision for a brand new routine. After wasting all that time, I would feel overwhelmed by the amount of effort required to settle into my new schedule... and I couldn't even manage to start. Delete the schedule, delete the app, download another, and start the maddening cycle all over again. Those days are gone, thanks to Routinery!
author: Praisegod Barebones

title: A great app for me, despite the bugs
text:
I have ADHD that I would say falls somewhere between “inconvenient” and “crippling.” Part of living with ADHD is figuring out what one is bad at, and personally I am bad at keeping lists of things in my head. So to keep things running at home, I have to-do routines that I do every morning. I used to use the Productive app for this, but the more cutesy that app got the more it distracted me. (I don’t need to be reminded to drink water, I need an app that yells at me until I do the dishes.) I searched around and found Routinery, and I think it’s very good at what it does. Its UI is simple, perhaps a little unconventional for an iOS app, but it does what it says on the tin, and that’s what matters. 

My only reservations about recommending this to others lie in the fact that the app is buggy on my 12” iPad. Sometimes it will spin forever while opening, and sometimes it will crash out of nowhere. However, the devs have been very good at ensuring my to-do list doesn’t lose progress, even if there is a crash. These are the kinds of failures that a dev can fix (I used to write apps, a long time ago) so I’m sure they will be fixed in the future. In the meantime, this app is very helpful in keeping me in sync with my chores and responsibilities.

title: Life-changing
text:
I’ve always struggled getting out the door on time for appointments, work, anything really. Part of ADHD is time perception dysfunction. We literally perceive time differently and have difficulty judging how long it actually takes to do things or knowing how much time has passed while performing a task. 

The app Routinery (iPhone) was a game changer for me. You create a routine (e.g. “Get ready for work”), and break it down into individual tasks. Then you put them in order and assign an amount of time for each. When you “run” the routine, your phone buzzes and prompts you each step of the way, and also updates your estimated end time based on how long it takes you to actually perform each task. So my AM routine literally starts with “take pills - 1 min” and then “stretch - 2 min”. Shower is next, and if I want to skip it because I showered the night before, then I skip it and it prompts me to do the next task which also updates the expected end time to show I’ll be done early. So maybe I end up taking a little longer to do my “makeup - 10 min” task. It buzzes that my time is up, but continues running the clock so I can see a) how much time I’m going over the expected time, and b) that I will still be done with my routine by whatever o’clock or that I will be late if I don’t skip something else later in the routine. 

I have been amaaaazed at how quickly I can actually do certain things when I am not constantly distracted by multitasking, and also not constantly checking my clock because I’m convinced that I’m going to be late if I don’t pay attention to the time. So it has allowed me to actually take time for meditation or checking emails or spending more time on my makeup, etc because I know for sure that I’ll be able to leave on time and I’m not just guessing. 

The other major use I have for it is a few routines I call “day off chores” and “deep clean”, etc. I created routines where I not only list tasks to do, but also include prep or transition time. Also, by deciding on a logical order of tasks ahead of time, I don’t get stuck in the never ending wheel of no accomplishment that ADHDers are famous for. Example: cleaning the bathroom. One task is just gathering rugs and towels and putting them in the wash. Then, scrubbing the toilet because the cleaner can soak in the bowl for a bit while I do the next thing. I have a task just for taking things off the bathroom counter, before the next task of wiping the counter and sink. It continues like this and it seems crazy but it ensures that I don’t get distracted and the most amazing thing is realizing that after programming a whole routine and adding the times I expect each task to take, the actual time is so much less than I assumed it would take. Before, sometimes cleaning the bathroom ends up being an all-day journey and for that reason I justify avoiding doing it. But if I know that I can deep clean my bathroom in about 20 min, it suddenly becomes super possible and satisfying. 

My day off routine includes things like “take a walk - 20 min” and “drink water” interspersed with productive tasks. It’s incredible how often I convince myself that I’m don’t have time to do things for myself and my mental health because im too busy. But by programming it into the routine, not only am I not worried about losing focus and getting back to productivity, but I don’t feel guilty about having “me time” because it’s considered just another task and I know I can fit it into the time I have. 

It is free to download but there is a price to use the app.  I think you can try it free for a time and then pay monthly, or annually. But honestly, about $20 for a year of life-changing task-prompting is worth it to me. 

Alllllllso, it’s notifications sync to my Fitbit so I don’t need to worry about having my phone in front of me and getting distracted while I’m going through my tasks. Just another thing that makes it awesome. 

Best of luck to you!

title: Tired of the Subscription Model
text:
I was really excited about this app as I’ve been looking for a quality routine app for quite some time. I downloaded this and I’m impressed with everything about it. Except the subscription model….

I understand the benefits for the developer to utilize a subscription model, but it rarely makes sense from a consumer point unless the service is absolutely necessary or highly valued. Even then, I can’t have 50 monthly subscriptions for every app on my phone. That’s just not realistic.

I would love to pay for this app though. If there was a one time purchase option I would pay it. Even if the price was more than a typical apple store app. Further, I would likely even pay for upgraded versions as changes are made over time. I just simply cannot and will not pay for another subscription service. My budget and time are limited and my month-to-month changes. Subscriptions, regardless of how small the price, pile up quickly.

Thank you.

title: Absolutely Life-Changing for ADHD
text:
I have struggled with time my entire life. Waking up late, getting to places late, going to bed late, etc. This app seems almost too good to be true and has changed my life in a matter of 24 hours using it for my morning and night routine. Allowing myself to realize how much time everything will actually take and giving me an ETA of sorts that gets pushed back whenever I take longer on a task is just revolutionary for my severe lack of time concept. 

The ONLY thing that could make it better is if I could link a routine within a routine. For example, I usually shower in the morning, but not always, and I have curly hair with a multi-step shower routine. Therefore, I'd like to have a shower routine saved in the app as an individual routine for any time, and also be able to link it within my morning routine. If this would be possible, it would be virtually a perfect app in my mind. Thank you so much for creating it and promise me it'll always be this good because I can honestly see myself using it forever :)

title: Changed my life
text:
This app allows me to plan out my mornings ahead of time so I don’t have to think of all the steps to my routine in the moment when I’m groggy!! So many times it has saved me from forgetting to do something important. 
I love it because you can allot the amount of time that tasks take you (a best guess is fine bc you can see how much time that task usually takes you over a few weeks and adjust it accordingly so it’s accurate) and then seeing everything together, you know exactly when you will be finished with the routine, so you don’t have to be stressed like “oh I don’t have time to do all these things” because you know you have time for it!
It takes so much mental load and energy off. 
I think there are some improvements that can be made, but it’s a really great product & if you’re like me and have been struggling with to-do lists and trying to keep track of all the steps of a routine, I highly recommend you try Routinery.

title: Only routine app that doesn’t enrage
text:
I’m ADHD and ASD. I have issues with being told what to do. Routines and authorities can trigger fury for me. This app works. I don’t get mad when it calmly reminds me, because it’s MY routine and I’ve chosen this. Every time I think, meh maybe I don’t need to be reminded, I forget something and head back to the app. I love planning a new routine when I’m calm and in the right headspace and then I can do the new routine on autopilot knowing I worked it out when I was in a good place. 

One thing! I would LOVE to be able to run two routines at once. Like have my long all day food routine overlap the morning and afternoon routines. Please work on that! xx

title: Is this the best app I’ve ever downloaded?
text:
I’m not prone to exaggerating so please believe me when I say this really might be the best app I’ve ever downloaded. The creators have clearly put a lot of thought into how it works and making it as simple as possible. Here are some things I’ve done since downloading the app:
Left the house on time
Left the house early
Developed new habits and routines without even thinking about it
Done the housework and done it quickly 
Packed my bag and got out of the house without losing anything 

If you struggle with these things you will know how amazing it is to be able to do them. I think the big difference from using an alarm or reminders is the sequencing and moving you from one thing to another. It also really helps when you’re overwhelmed by having so many things to do. I found it really odd for the first few mornings I used it because I’m not used to doing one thing after another without stopping and thinking or getting lost or overwhelmed. 

Developers - if you could change one very small thing it would be to easily reorder several items in the list rather than having to reorder them one at a time. But seriously, what an amazing app.

title: Best Routine App Available!!
text: I love this app! I love the structure, I love the imagery. I love that it tracks streaks, I love that it reminds you and even has a voice reminder when ur looking away from your phone. I like the interface, it’s the BEST compared to a lot of other routine apps. As someone who’s struggling to follow their paper planner and paper written routines, having it visible on the phone with a timer and an estimated finishing time has been so helpful. I’ve been able to properly gauge how much time I have left to do things and whether I have to skip a task etc. it’s been helping me with establishing a solid routine for myself. I love it. However, there’s one thing that I don’t love. I don’t love that it’s a subscription. For this kind of app, I feel like a subscription is kinda… bogus. I understand that creators want to be compensated for their work, but ever since every service shifted to subscriptions it’s been a pain to even think about adding one. It seems so cheap at first, but add the cost of your streaming services(Netflix, Hulu, Spotify), business services(Microsoft, trello,wix, etc.), other apps(Apple +, Fitbit +, etc), tangible services(gym memberships, dance lessons, piano lessons etc.) . It’s like everyone wants to make MORE money these days for services that should have a FLAT COST and it’s getting ridiculous. I mean how can all these creators expect us to hold all these different subscriptions? I will say, the subscription is CHEAP and that’s nice. But if I’m being honest, I don’t think it’s a service worth subscribing to. At that point I’d rather retry the pen and paper and see how far I get. However, I DO think that it deserves compensation. That’s actually what I was preparing to do before writing this review. I think that the app needs to have an option for a FLAT COST that allows the user to buy access to all the features for lifetime. If you were giving me LIFETIME access to the features, I’d be willing to go up to maybe $60 just to be able to get ALL the features for a lifetime because this app has really helped me.  Some people prefer subscriptions and will pay, but for those of us that don’t see a point in subscribing to an app with basic but helpful functions(or those who already have too many subscriptions), please give us a FLAT COST that allows us to compensate you in the method we may best see fit. Thank you

title: 무조건 추천하는 앱!!!
text:
모닝 루틴을 습관화해보려고 시작한 앱인데 너무너무 좋습니다. 우선 타이머가 시키는 대로 아무 생각 없이, 쉴 틈 없이 움직이고 행동하다 보면 마지막에 ‘수고하셨습니다’하고 말해주는데 그 한마디가 오늘도 해냈다 칭찬받는 기분이 듭니다. 또 제가 너무너무 이 앱을 좋아하는 이유이자 리뷰 작성까지 마음먹은 이유는 상단에 뜨는 대화들 때문입니다. 매번 뜨는 대화가 다른데 기분 탓이겠지만^^; 그날에 저에게 필요한 말들이 떠서 위로를 받습니다. 어떤 날은 피드를 당겨 문장이 바뀌는 걸 여러 번 읽고 루틴을 시작하기도 합니다. 정말 좋은 말들이 많이 뜨고 따뜻한 말들이 매번 저를 응원해 줍니다. 늦잠 잤을 때도 포기할 수 없는, 가장 가까이에서 가장 쉽게 나를 보살필 수 있는 앱입니다.❤️너무너무 감사합니다!!
(이유는 모르겠지만 오류나서 3번 작성하는 리뷰입니다. 그 정도로 개좋아..)

title: App keeps shutting down
text:
I downloaded this app this morning and I absolutely loved it. I added a morning routine and I got everything done, I absolutely loved the timing features. 
I went to create a new routine after the gym and the app said I need to purchase the subscription. No problem - I loved the app so much this morning I would spend whatever they asked. I make the 6 month purchase and when I go to add a new routine, it tells me I need to subscribe…
I purchased probably 7 subscriptions, all different levels and nothing worked. The app became so so so glitchy after one use. The screen froze, I subscribed muiltple times and it kept telling me I need to subscribe. 
I turn my phone off and back on. Deleted the app and redownloaded it twice. Logged out and back it. Created a new account and subscribed AGAIN.  Nothing has resolved the issue. 
I have never written a review for an app before but I liked the app so much and it is now completely unusable. 
This app is meant to help you stay on task and focused but I have wasted hours just trying to use it.

title: Grateful for this app!!
text: I really love this app!! It’s simple in the best way - I actually look forward to using it because it doesn’t add to my overwhelm, but it helps guide me and implement the routines that I know help but have a hard time sticking to. The fact that I can skip a single task, rearrange it, or even get a check for my routine even if I didn’t finish everything 100% is very helpful to countering the perfectionism that often ends up hurting my ability to keep returning. As someone with ADHD, There is a good balance of affirmation and discipline here and I’m grateful for it since most other apps don’t have that balance. Thank you!!

title: Wow. Just wow!
text:
I downloaded this app to help with executive function issues related to ADHD and anxiety. It’s been only a few days but it has changed my life for the better! 

I couldn’t get things done in a timely manner and I found myself very overwhelmed. I’ve been using this app for about 4 days and I feel like a different person. I’ve taken care of myself, cleaned my house, meal prepped, and even exercised. And it was all because this app let me do things in order without me having to worry about remembering to do this thing or the other. 

For me, the process of remembering each and every task and step causes me to not be able to turn off my thoughts while doing a given task. With Routinery, I know the app is going to tell me what to do next so I can focus on the task at hand. Wow. Just wow!

title: Great app, and here’s a suggestion
text:
I already posted a 5 star review for this wonderful app, and I maintain my high regard.

I would also like to make an additional suggestion:
Would it be possible to add the option to make some routines play-as-needed rather than on repeat the same time everyday? For example, I’d like to set a routine for packing a bag to work remotely at the park. The items in the bag are consistent and Routinery would help me get it done quickly, not forgetting anything, but I don’t need this routine at a consistent time every week. The same goes for certain work out routines. I’m also a dog sitter and my routine changes when I’m getting up super early to walk dogs, but that only lasts for about a week at a time. The point is that temporary routines can be useful.
I am already loving this app and I use it for my regular morning and evening routines. I just think adding the option to use certain routines at irregular times would make it even better.
author: ginormousgiant

title: A winner for my neurodivergent brain
text:
I used Tiimo before but wasn’t super happy with it (personal preferences). I also had issues with it working consistently with my Apple Watch. After downloading and deleting several other routine apps I found Routinery. It has been fantastic. 

 *Things I like:*

-  It has a clean and minimalistic design. It clicked with my brain right away 
- Creating a new routine is a quick and easy process You can update an existing routine without any excess steps 
- Everything is clearly labeled
- The font and buttons are large enough to navigate with ease 
- You are able to duplicate a routine. This is handy for me when my routine changes by one activity on a given day. For example, on Sundays my closing duties routine is the same but with the addition of filling my pillbox for the upcoming week. It's nice to not have to create a whole new routine from scratch
- There are a variety of settings to make it customized to my needs - timer settings, settings for improved concentration, and add-ons like haptic vibration and status bar
- There is a timer setting under Push Notifications called "Pause Timer Notification" that you can turn on. If it's on it will notify you 5, 10, and/or 20 minutes after you pause an activity in a routine to remind you that it's paused 
- There's an option to not automatically go to the next activity(!!!) 
- It has worked seamlessly with my Apple Watch thus far which is a must for me 

*Things I dislike:*  
- I'd like the option to view individual days rather than just Today 

Clearly a winner for me!

title: A wonderful app!
text:
I’ve been using Routinery for a few months now and it’s been very helpful 

I have ADHD and I just forget to look after my bod. A lot of the time it’s just because I have a really bad concept of time and think I don’t have time to look after myself 

Also my little dog has worked out that if she taps my phone screen with her nose she will make breakfast happen quicker 😂😂😂 

But I’ve got my morning routine down now to work on my bedtime one ha 

I do have some possibly improvements

- let me change the colour of the clock face timer. Instead of dark grey on white as if my phone is across the room on charge it’s hard to see how much time I have without breaking focus 

- quick add tasks . Sometimes I might realise while I’m walking my dog that I have extra time before I need to leave for work to do laundry to do or washing up. It would be nice to have a list of maybe 10-15 for quick add tasks . Because when I have to exit and the write the task I get distracted 

-some of the wording I find a little confusing.

You currently have buttons that say this:
“Redo after rest” and “redo from the time ended”

But I think this phrasing is less confusing :
“Restart last task” and “Continue with last task”

title: Easy routine app for neurodiverse people!!
text:
Routinery is a very convenient way to organise your day & is still very useful without the premium option unlike other routine apps I've tried!! 

Pros I've noticed: 
- Being able to change the order of your routine activities while you're completing them is very helpful.
- The voice notifications are a great feature to helps me complete my routine without having to look at my phone & helps me get ready faster.

Cons i've noticed: 
- The app is very blinding in the mornings when I'm still trying to wake up. I wish they would make a dark mode setting for the app. 
- The volume of the voice notifications are extremely loud some days & doesnt change when I change my volume settings like the app suggests.

Overall routinery is one of the best routine apps I've tried. I have used the app for more than 3 months (which says a lot) and haven't had to delete it straight away because the in-app purchases make it unusable!! I would appreciate them making a dark mode setting 💞
